components.gap: The route presents Theorems 1-6, the Sec. 2.2 lemma, the Sec. 1-4 definitions, the de Bruijn attribution and the closing questions with written proofs (Theorem 6 by a marker/template construction), and the graph consequence (rado-1964.tex 79-103), but these claims of the complete article (Rado 1964, pp. 331-340, held scan read in full) are not presented: (1) Sec. 4.1, p. 337: 'We recall the definition of Tarski's cofinality function cf(n)', cf(n) being the least ordinal such that aleph_n is a sum of aleph_cf(n) cardinals smaller than aleph_n; hbconvention def:p03-rado64-transfinite-indices (rado-1964.tex 255-269) calls it 'Rado's index-valued notation', omits the Tarski attribution, and replaces the source's sum-of-smaller-cardinals definition by cf(aleph_n)=aleph_cf(n) without stating the source's form or the equivalence. (2) Sec. 4.2, p. 337: 'Without loss of generality we may assume m to be an initial ordinal'; this source remark replacing the hypothesis on m is not reported; rado-1964.tex 286-295 and annex 4-23 assert that no transfer is assumed and prove that F(2,omega+1,{0,1}) has no universal member, but never identify the source's stated reduction or record that this boundary theorem bears on it. (3) Sec. 2.1, p. 333 ('Graphs are one-dimensional simplicial complexes') and Sec. 3, p. 335 ('Theorem 1 is concerned with K21, Theorem 3 with K2l, and Theorem 4 with K2'; Theorem 5 'is a generalization of Theorems 1, 3 and 4'); rado-1964.tex 243 says only 'The binary complexes are the k=2 cases', so graphs/Theorem 1 as the K21 case and Theorem 5 as generalizing Theorem 1 are not stated. (4) Smaller remarks: Sec. 1.1, p. 331, the intersection of two distinct edges is empty or a single point; n. 4, p. 333, only 'into' is needed where the Lemma is applied.
components.basis: Present and compared: intro and the de Bruijn attribution (rado-1964.tex 5-17, 118-125); Sec. 1.1 graph, weak and induced embedding, the {0,1} example and (weak) universality (22-39); Theorem 1 with the high-digit recursion (41-70, annex 38-58); Sec. 1.2 local finiteness, tree, k(Gamma,x,m) and Theorem 2 with the diagonal choice p_m = k(H,m,m) (108-122, annex 116-139); Lemma 2.2 with the consecutive-rank telescoping (130-147, annex 142-168); Theorems 3 and 4 incl. the l=0 footnote and the singleton case (155-206, annex 171-221); Sec. 3 classes K_kl, K_k, Theorem 5(a)(b), representations (6) and (7), and the mod-k/oriented-simplex reading (211-246, annex 223-263); Sec. 4.2 reduction (297-303, annex 266-277); Theorem 6 cases (i)-(iii) under 2^aleph_nu = aleph_(nu+1) with full proof (325-351, annex 280-447); the closing questions (353-356). Failure condition not triggered: induced embeddings are fixed (26-33), the deterministic graph is stated not to be a distribution on finite graphs (103), and the extension/uniqueness claims carry written proofs (annex 61-91).

Binary-digit graph R on N_0 (rado-1964.tex 41-57); induced (edge- and nonedge-preserving) universality for every graph with at most countably many vertices by the high-digit recursion, finite and empty inputs included (59-70, annex 38-58); every disjoint finite U,V extension instance with witnesses z_M = 2^M + sum over U of 2^u, empty cases included, infinitely many witnesses (79-89, annex 63-70); back-and-forth uniqueness and homogeneity with written forward and backward stages (annex 72-84); identification with the Fraisse graph limit, which also embeds every countable graph as an induced subgraph (annex 86-91; fraisse-1954.tex 416-430, annex 627-663).

Free amalgam of finite simple graphs over a common induced subgraph and an explicit AP failure for finite forests (induced paths a-x-b and a-y-z-b forcing the cycle a-x-b-z-y-a) at rado-1964.tex 91-99 and annex 94-113; further explicit amalgams (relations, linear orders, partial orders with the Fig. 1 cycle) and the ramified-order failure of Fig. 2 at fraisse-1954.tex 281-341 and annex 406-458; structural embeddings distinguished from partial elementary maps at rado-1964.tex 101-103, fraisse-1954.tex 210-212 and def:p03-ultrahomogeneous (classification-theory.tex 54-64).
